document.title: Dealing with the Taliban in Kabul
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] After the Taliban takeover of Kabul, State instructs the Embassy in Pakistan to engage the new Taliban interim government on stability, human rights, narcotics and terrorism. Talking points show the desire to locate Osama Bin Laden.

events.description: State Department cable instructs US Embassy Islamabad on initial contacts with the Taliban interim government in Kabul.
Taliban forces entered Kabul, violated UN premises and summarily executed former President Najibullah.

SECSTATE (Christopher) cable instructs Embassy Islamabad and Consulate Peshawar on talking points for initial contact with the Taliban interim government in Kabul, covering a broad-based government, narcotics, terrorism, and bin Laden.
The US asks the Taliban about the status of the training camps formerly run by Hekmatyar, Sayyaf or Arab groups, and about bin Laden's location.
The US pledged USD 1.6 million through UNDCP over the last two years for counter-narcotics work in Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: The US cable cites the summary execution of former President Najibullah by Taliban forces.
relationships.quote: THE VIOLATION OF UN PREMISES WHEN YOUR FORCES ENTERED KABUL AND BY THE SUMMARY EXECUTION OF FORMER PRESIDENT NAJIBULLAH.

relationships.detail: US seeks early engagement with the Taliban interim government.
relationships.quote: WE WISH TO ENGAGE THE NEW TALIBAN "INTERIM GOVERNMENT" AT AN EARLY STAGE

relationships.detail: US had heard bin Laden was in the eastern provinces.
relationships.quote: WE HAD HEARD PREVIOUSLY THAT HE WAS IN THE EASTERN PROVINCES.

relationships.detail: Camps are described as formerly run by Hekmatyar; his group is implied.
relationships.quote: TRAINING CAMPS FORMERLY RUN BY HEKMATYAR, SAYYAFP OR ARAB GROUPS

relationships.detail: Camps are described as formerly run by Sayyaf; his group is implied.
relationships.quote: TRAINING CAMPS FORMERLY RUN BY HEKMATYAR, SAYYAFP OR ARAB GROUPS

relationships.detail: Raphel is Assistant Secretary of the Bureau of South Asian Affairs at the State Department and classified the cable.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY ROBIN L. RAPHEL, ASSISTANT SECRETARY, BUREAU OF SOUTH ASIAN AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF STATE.

relationships.detail: The cable from SECSTATE is signed CHRISTOPHER, the Secretary of State.
relationships.quote: CHRISTOPHER

relationships.detail: The Taliban now control Kabul and much of the country.
relationships.quote: WE RECOGNIZE THAT THE TALIBAN NOW CONTROL KABUL AND MUCH OF THE COUNTRY.

relationships.detail: The US urges the Taliban to work closely with the UN, whose premises the Taliban violated on entering Kabul.
relationships.quote: WE URGE YOU TO CONTINUE TO WORK CLOSELY WITH THEM.

relationships.detail: The US pledged USD 1.6 million through UNDCP for counter-narcotics work in Afghanistan, so the US is the funder. Direction is recorded as stated in the schema, but the US is the provider.
relationships.quote: WE HAVE PLEDGED USDOLS 1.6 MILLION THRU UNDCP OVER THE LAST 2 YEARS FOR THEIR WORK IN AFGHANISTAN.

relationships.quote: TERRORIST AND MILITANT TRAINING CAMPS FORMERLY RUN BY HEKMATYAR, SAYYAFP OR ARAB GROUPS.

relationships.detail: Sayyaf is associated with the militant training camps the Taliban said they were closing.
relationships.quote: TERRORIST AND MILITANT TRAINING CAMPS FORMERLY RUN BY HEKMATYAR, SAYYAFP OR ARAB GROUPS.

relationships.detail: Hekmatyar formerly ran terrorist and militant training camps in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: CLOSING THE TERRORIST AND MILITANT TRAINING CAMPS FORMERLY RUN BY HEKMATYAR, SAYYAFP OR ARAB GROUPS.

relationships.detail: The US had heard that bin Laden was in the Eastern provinces of Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: WE HAD HEARD PREVIOUSLY THAT HE WAS IN THE EASTERN PROVINCES.

relationships.detail: The Eastern provinces are part of Afghanistan, where bin Laden's presence was said not to serve Afghan interests.
relationships.quote: HIS CONTINUED PRESENCE HERE WOULD NOT, WE BELIEVE, SERVE AFGHANISTAN'S INTERESTS.

relationships.detail: Opium cultivation in Helmand has increased by over 30 percent each year since 1993.
relationships.quote: CULTIVATION IN HELMAND HAS INCREASED BY OVER 30

relationships.detail: Heroin processing in Kandahar has reportedly increased dramatically.
relationships.quote: HEROIN PROCESSING IN KANDAHAR HAS ALSO INCREASED DRAMATICALLY.

relationships.detail: The cable is addressed to Embassy Islamabad, which is to send representatives to Kabul.
relationships.quote: EMBASSY ISLAMABAD IS AUTHORIZED TO SEND REPRESENTATIVES TO KABUL

key_claims: The US sought early engagement with the Taliban interim government in Kabul to demonstrate willingness to deal with them as the new authorities.
The US prioritized a broad-based government, narcotics and terrorism as key concerns.
The Taliban had assured the US that they were closing terrorist training camps run by Hekmatyar, Sayyaf or Arab groups.
The US asked the Taliban about bin Laden's location and said his continued presence would not serve Afghanistan's interests.
The US cited rising opium cultivation in Helmand and heroin processing in Kandahar.
The US said reopening its Kabul embassy was under review, subject to security.
